subject: Digital Image Processing

programs.question: Write program to read and display digital image using Python
programs.aim: Become familiar with basic image processing commands and libraries in Python; read and display, resize, convert, inspect, separate, merge, and write image data.

subExercises.question: Become familiar with Basic image processing commands and libraries in Python
Read and display image in Python
Convert given color image into gray-scale image
Convert given color/gray-scale image into black & white image
Separate color image in three R G & B planes
Create color image using R, G and B three separate planes
Write given 2-D data in image file

answer.code:
from PIL import Image
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

img = Image.open(r"C:\Users\samit\Downloads\images.jpg")
a = np.array(img)
g = np.array(img.convert("L"))
bw = (g > 128) * 255
row = g[g.shape[0] // 2]
res = img.resize((200, 200))
data = np.tile(np.linspace(0, 255, 200), (200, 1)).astype(np.uint8)

# R, G, B isolated images
chans = []
for i in range(3):
    c = np.zeros_like(a)
    c[:, :, i] = a[:, :, i]
    chans.append(c)

items = [img, res, g, bw, row, chans[0], chans[1], chans[2], a, data]
titles = ["Original", "Resize", "Gray", "B/W", "Profile", "R", "G", "B", "Merge", "2D"]
cmaps = [None, None, "gray", "gray", None, None, None, None, None, "gray"]

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
for i in range(10):
    plt.subplot(3, 4, i + 1)
    plt.title(titles[i])
    if titles[i] == "Profile":
        plt.plot(items[i])
    else:
        plt.imshow(items[i], cmap=cmaps[i])
        plt.axis("off")

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

programs.question: To write and execute image processing programs using point processing method
programs.aim: Obtain negative and flipped images, perform thresholding, and apply contrast stretching.

answer.code:
import cv2
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

img = cv2.cvtColor(cv2.imread(r"C:\Users\samit\Downloads\IMG20260813082043.jpg"),
                   cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
gray = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_RGB2GRAY)
neg = 255 - gray
flip = cv2.flip(img, 1)
th = cv2.threshold(gray, 127, 255, cv2.THRESH_BINARY)[1]
cs = cv2.normalize(gray, None, 0, 255, cv2.NORM_MINMAX)

plt.subplot(2,3,1); plt.imshow(img); plt.title("Original"); plt.axis("off")
plt.subplot(2,3,2); plt.imshow(neg, cmap="gray"); plt.title("Negative"); plt.axis("off")
plt.subplot(2,3,3); plt.imshow(flip); plt.title("Flip"); plt.axis("off")
plt.subplot(2,3,4); plt.imshow(th, cmap="gray"); plt.title("Threshold"); plt.axis("off")
plt.subplot(2,3,5); plt.imshow(cs, cmap="gray"); plt.title("Contrast"); plt.axis("off")
plt.show()

import cv2, numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

a = cv2.cvtColor(cv2.imread(r"C:\Users\samit\Downloads\IMG20260813082043.jpg"),
                 cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)

programs.question: To write and execute programs for image logical operations
programs.aim: Perform AND, OR, intersection, and NOT operations on binary images.

subExercises.question: Calculate intersection of two images. NOT operation (Negative image)

answer.code:
import numpy as np
import cv2
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

img1 = np.zeros((300,300),np.uint8)
cv2.rectangle(img1,(50,50),(200,200),255,-1)
img2 = np.zeros((300,300),np.uint8)
cv2.circle(img2,(180,180),100,255,-1)

and_img = cv2.bitwise_and(img1,img2)
or_img = cv2.bitwise_or(img1,img2)
not_img = cv2.bitwise_not(img1)

plt.subplot(2,3,1); plt.imshow(img1,cmap='gray'); plt.title("A"); plt.axis("off")
plt.subplot(2,3,2); plt.imshow(img2,cmap='gray'); plt.title("B"); plt.axis("off")
plt.subplot(2,3,3); plt.imshow(and_img,cmap='gray'); plt.title("AND"); plt.axis("off")
plt.subplot(2,3,4); plt.imshow(or_img,cmap='gray'); plt.title("OR"); plt.axis("off")
plt.subplot(2,3,5); plt.imshow(not_img,cmap='gray'); plt.title("NOT"); plt.axis("off")
plt.show()

programs.question: To write a program for histogram calculation and equalization
programs.aim: Calculate an image histogram using a standard function and a manual loop, and perform histogram equalization.

answer.code:
import cv2
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

img = cv2.imread(r"C:\Users\samit\Downloads\IMG20260813082043.jpg", 0)

# Standard method
hist = cv2.calcHist([img],[0],None,[256],[0,256])
eq = cv2.equalizeHist(img)

# Without function (simple loop)
h = np.zeros(256)
for i in img.flatten():
    h[i] += 1

# Display
plt.subplot(2,2,1); plt.imshow(img,cmap="gray"); plt.title("Image"); plt.axis("off")
plt.subplot(2,2,2); plt.plot(hist); plt.title("Hist")
plt.subplot(2,2,3); plt.imshow(eq,cmap="gray"); plt.title("Equalized"); plt.axis("off")
plt.subplot(2,2,4); plt.plot(h); plt.title("Manual Hist")
plt.show()

programs.question: To write and execute program for geometric transformation of image
programs.aim: Apply translation, scaling, rotation, shrinking, and zooming to an image.

answer.code:
import cv2
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

img = cv2.cvtColor(cv2.imread(r"C:\Users\samit\Downloads\IMG20260813082043.jpg"),
                   cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
r, c = img.shape[:2]

# Translation matrix (FIXED PART)
M = np.float32([[1, 0, 80],
                [0, 1, 50]])
t = cv2.warpAffine(img, M, (c, r))

# Other operations
s = cv2.resize(img, None, fx=1.5, fy=1.5)
sh = cv2.resize(img, None, fx=0.5, fy=0.5)
z = cv2.resize(img, None, fx=2, fy=2)
rot = cv2.warpAffine(img, cv2.getRotationMatrix2D((c/2, r/2), 45, 1), (c, r))

# Display
plt.subplot(2,3,1); plt.imshow(img); plt.title("Original"); plt.axis("off")
plt.subplot(2,3,2); plt.imshow(t); plt.title("Translate"); plt.axis("off")
plt.subplot(2,3,3); plt.imshow(s); plt.title("Scale"); plt.axis("off")
plt.subplot(2,3,4); plt.imshow(rot); plt.title("Rotate"); plt.axis("off")
plt.subplot(2,3,5); plt.imshow(sh); plt.title("Shrink"); plt.axis("off")
plt.subplot(2,3,6); plt.imshow(z); plt.title("Zoom"); plt.axis("off")
plt.show()

programs.question: To understand various image noise models and to write programs for
programs.aim: Demonstrate image restoration, salt-and-pepper noise removal, Gaussian noise reduction, and median filtering.

answer.code:
import cv2
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

img = cv2.imread(r"C:\Users\samit\Downloads\IMG20260813082043.jpg", 0)
sp = img.copy()
sp[50:80,50:80] = 255
sp[120:150,120:150] = 0
median = cv2.medianBlur(sp, 5)
g = img + np.random.normal(0,20,img.shape)
g = np.clip(g,0,255).astype(np.uint8)
gauss = cv2.GaussianBlur(g,(5,5),0)

plt.subplot(2,3,1); plt.imshow(img,cmap="gray"); plt.title("Org"); plt.axis("off")
plt.subplot(2,3,2); plt.imshow(sp,cmap="gray"); plt.title("SP"); plt.axis("off")
plt.subplot(2,3,3); plt.imshow(median,cmap="gray"); plt.title("Med"); plt.axis("off")
plt.subplot(2,3,4); plt.imshow(g,cmap="gray"); plt.title("Gaus"); plt.axis("off")
plt.subplot(2,3,5); plt.imshow(gauss,cmap="gray"); plt.title("Filt"); plt.axis("off")
plt.show()

programs.question: Write and execute programs for image frequency domain filtering
programs.aim: Apply FFT, perform low-pass and high-pass filtering in the frequency domain, and use IFFT to reconstruct filtered images.

subExercises.question: Perform low pass and high pass filtering in frequency domain

answer.code:
import cv2, numpy as np, matplotlib.pyplot as plt

img = cv2.imread(r"C:\Users\samit\Downloads\images.jpg", 0)
f = np.fft.fftshift(np.fft.fft2(img))
mag = 20*np.log(np.abs(f)+1)

r,c = img.shape
cr,cc = r//2,c//2
rad = 60

# LPF
lpf = np.zeros((r,c),np.uint8)
cv2.circle(lpf,(cc,cr),rad,1,-1)
lpf_img = np.abs(np.fft.ifft2(np.fft.ifftshift(f*lpf)))

# HPF
hpf = np.ones((r,c),np.uint8)
cv2.circle(hpf,(cc,cr),rad,0,-1)
hpf_img = np.abs(np.fft.ifft2(np.fft.ifftshift(f*hpf)))

# Normalize
lpf_img = cv2.normalize(lpf_img,None,0,255,cv2.NORM_MINMAX).astype(np.uint8)
hpf_img = cv2.normalize(hpf_img,None,0,255,cv2.NORM_MINMAX).astype(np.uint8)

# Display
imgs = [img, mag, lpf, lpf_img, hpf, hpf_img]
titles = ["Original","FFT","LPF Mask","LPF Output","HPF Mask","HPF Output"]
for i in range(6):
    plt.subplot(2,3,i+1)
    plt.imshow(imgs[i], cmap='gray')
    plt.title(titles[i]); plt.axis('off')

plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

programs.question: Write a program for edge detection using different edge detection masks.
programs.aim: Detect image edges using Sobel, Prewitt, Roberts, and Canny methods.

answer.code:
import cv2
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

img = cv2.imread(r"C:\Users\samit\Downloads\IMG20260813082043.jpg", 0)
sobel = cv2.Sobel(img, cv2.CV_64F, 1, 1, 3)
prewitt = cv2.filter2D(img, -1,
                       np.array([[-1,0,1],
                                 [-1,0,1],
                                 [-1,0,1]]))
roberts = cv2.filter2D(img, -1,
                       np.array([[1,0],
                                 [0,-1]]))
canny = cv2.Canny(img, 100, 200)

plt.subplot(2,3,1); plt.imshow(img,cmap="gray"); plt.title("Org"); plt.axis("off")
plt.subplot(2,3,2); plt.imshow(sobel,cmap="gray"); plt.title("Sobel"); plt.axis("off")
plt.subplot(2,3,3); plt.imshow(prewitt,cmap="gray"); plt.title("Prewitt"); plt.axis("off")
plt.subplot(2,3,4); plt.imshow(roberts,cmap="gray"); plt.title("Roberts"); plt.axis("off")
plt.subplot(2,3,5); plt.imshow(canny,cmap="gray"); plt.title("Canny"); plt.axis("off")
plt.show()

programs.question: Write and execute program for image morphological operations erosion and dilation.
programs.aim: Perform erosion and dilation on a thresholded binary image.

answer.code:
import cv2
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

img = cv2.imread(r"C:\Users\samit\Downloads\IMG20260813082043.jpg", 0)
_, b = cv2.threshold(img, 127, 255, 0)
k = np.ones((5,5), np.uint8)
e = cv2.erode(b, k)
d = cv2.dilate(b, k)

plt.subplot(1,3,1); plt.imshow(b,cmap="gray"); plt.title("Binary"); plt.axis("off")
plt.subplot(1,3,2); plt.imshow(e,cmap="gray"); plt.title("Erode"); plt.axis("off")
plt.subplot(1,3,3); plt.imshow(d,cmap="gray"); plt.title("Dilate"); plt.axis("off")
plt.show()
